_note: The war diary (release 2; Brian's yes of 27 November 2026 13:40Z to the playtester's idea). src/campaign/diary.ts. As the player's month opens, one entry is set down for the month gone: its biggest win and its worst loss among the land battles his own corps fought, in the voice of a diary kept at the time. Words only: no rule reads it. 'keep': the most entries the war keeps (the oldest go first). 'shown': the most the diary page shows. 'round': the numbers in an entry are rounded to this.
win: The best news came from {place}: {unit} beat the {adj} soundly, and some {theirs} of theirs are dead, wounded or in our cages.
{place} is the name on every lip in the mess tonight. {unit} saw the {adj} off and brought in {prisoners} prisoners.
A good day at {place}. {unit} stood up to the {adj} and gave rather better than it got: some {theirs} of theirs for {ours} of ours.
They will be ringing bells for {place} at home. {unit} sent the {adj} back the way they came.
loss: The black spot was {place}, where {unit} was roughly handled and some {ours} of our men did not come back.
Against that, {place}. {unit} was driven back, and the casualty lists will be long.
But {place} went badly: {unit} lost some {ours} men there, and nobody in the mess is saying much about it.
The worst of it was {place}. The {adj} were too strong for {unit}, and we paid for it with some {ours} men.
noWin: No victory to set against it.
Nothing to cheer about this month.
noLoss: Nothing went badly enough to write down.
Not a reverse worth the name all month.
quiet: Quiet on every front. The men cleaned their rifles and wrote home.
Nothing to set down but the weather and the waiting.
No battle for our corps this month. The rumours did the fighting.
